assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins gave a quantitative, physically grounded account of how tunnelling through the polypeptide depends on distance and medium, tested with ruthenium-modified proteins and time-resolved kinetics. It underpins our understanding of respiration and photosynthesis, where electron and proton transfer are coupled across membranes. This is the kind of mechanism stated in physical terms that I value.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are a clear, compact pairing for the experimental programme of photo-triggered electron transfer in proteins and the tunnelling-pathway picture. Theory by others (Marcus already recognised in 1992; Beratan and Onuchic pathways) is related but need not be included; the scope of the cited theory work could be contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and widespread textbook use; no sign of premature recognition. The risk is the opposite: the field is old and part of it was already honoured via Marcus's 1992 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the Marcus-recognised electron transfer theory.
Relative credit of experimental versus theoretical contributions (e.g. pathway models) is not resolved from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyses biological N2 reduction, a central problem in bioinorganic chemistry. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and the FeMo-cofactor, the interstitial carbide, and work on the electron-transfer and substrate-binding cycle give a mechanistic picture of one of the hardest enzymatic reactions. Strong importance for energy-converting enzymes and for ammonia chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Structural work (Rees, Einsle) and biochemical/spectroscopic mechanism (Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe) are both decisive, so three places are tight. I propose Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, accepting that Dean and Ribbe have strong claims and that the biochemical-genetic and structural lines may be hard to separate.
assessment.maturity: The structure is well confirmed and widely reproduced; the catalytic cycle (E4 state, hydride chemistry, N2 binding site) is still being refined, so the mechanism is only partly settled.
uncertainties: The detailed mechanism of N2 reduction is not fully resolved.
Allocation among five credited names and a three-laureate limit is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a unifying concept for how charge moves in biology (respiratory enzymes, photosystem II) and in molecular electrocatalysis. Theory of concerted and sequential PCET with nonadiabatic proton tunnelling, together with experimental bond-weakening and thermochemical frameworks, converts a vague idea into predictive mechanism. Close to my own field, so I will weigh my own bias with care.
assessment.attribution: Hammes-Schiffer (theory), Mayer (concerted PCET thermodynamics and kinetics) and Nocera (PCET in water oxidation and artificial photosynthesis) form a plausible set, but Meyer's early contribution is real and the three-person limit forces a difficult cut.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across biology and catalysis; the conceptual framework is stable, though the more applied electrocatalysis side keeps evolving.
uncertainties: Risk that the candidacy is a broad line of work rather than a single clearly attributable discovery.
Priority between Meyer and the other named researchers is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, and the demonstrated effect was global through siRNA and mRNA vaccines. The chemistry of pH-dependent ionizable lipids and rapid-mixing formulation is a clear molecular-design contribution with enormous measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group was decisive in the lipid-particle formulation and the ionizable-lipid concept; Hope and Madden were central co-inventors in the early work. Others (MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) developed the lipid library and clinical translation, so credit is shared across several institutions.
assessment.maturity: Clinical and real-world confirmation is very strong. Timing is arguably favourable, though the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modification affects how the committee views the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine recognition of mRNA technology and how that shapes timing.
Intellectual property and priority disputes among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled diffraction before radiation damage, and time-resolved studies of reactions in crystals. It makes dynamic biochemical mechanisms visible, which I regard highly, with results on photosystem II, photoactive proteins and enzyme intermediates.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu's idea of diffraction before destruction, Chapman's experimental demonstration and method development, and Schlichting's and Fromme's biological applications all matter. I propose Chapman, Hajdu and Schlichting but the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The method is well established, but the most compelling mechanistic payoffs are still accumulating, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the biochemical discoveries are yet distinctive enough to justify the prize.
Allocation between methods inventors and application leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase, giving stoichiometry, subunit architecture and ligand binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins and lipid interactions. It is a widely used structural technique complementary to cryo-EM and crystallography.
assessment.attribution: Robinson (membrane proteins, ribosome and complexes), Chait and Heck are leading contributors, but Loo and Gross and the earlier ESI pioneers (already recognised in 2002) complicate the history of credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently validated; the field is mature, though a portion of its foundations falls under the 2002 ESI recognition.
uncertainties: Distinguishing contributions from the ESI work recognised in 2002.
Whether it is a methodology line rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and funnel picture explains how proteins fold quickly despite astronomical conformational space, and has been tested experimentally with kinetics and phi-value analysis. It is a physical principle for biomolecular behaviour that spans theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are central to the landscape theory, while Fersht made the key experimental mapping of folding transition states; Dill and Bryngelson also contributed. The combination is plausible but the theory-experiment boundary is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Concept widely accepted for decades; part of the field's later credit is shared with structure prediction successes (2024 prize), so timing may feel less urgent.
uncertainties: Effect of the 2024 Chemistry prize for protein design and structure prediction on perceived novelty.
Allocation of credit between landscape theory and experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes drug discovery by recruiting E3 ligases through bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, with a clear mechanistic basis in ubiquitin-proteasome biochemistry and clinical molecules in trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray and others advanced structure-based design. The set is plausible but the field has many valid claimants.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still maturing; the concept is confirmed, but long-term impact is less settled than the more established topics above.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes are not yet decisive.
